conceptZh: 早是太陽剛升起來的清晨
object: a boxy mismatched toy robot with one long arm and a huge cardboard sun
morph: the robot cranks a huge round sun up over a short post so that 日 sits on 十, forming 早
creativeAngle: 早字是「日」在「十」上，像太陽升在旗桿上；機器人的大太陽比自己還大，只好用那條長手臂撐住。詞用「早安」。
promptEn: An 8-second 3D animated toy clip on a clean solid pale sky-blue backdrop, locked camera. The only text is the single Traditional Chinese glyph 早, centered in saturated sunrise-orange strokes about 70 percent of frame height: a squarish 日 on top standing directly over the cross 十 below. Cast: a boxy toy robot named Bolt made of mismatched tin parts, with a rusty blue body, one arm much longer than the other, and a wind-up key in his back. Moment one, 0 to 1.8s: Bolt marches in from the left in a morning stretch, yawning with a squeaky creak, dragging a sun that is far too big, a glowing golden disc taller than he is, wrapped in a ribbon like a balloon. The first 早 is spoken as the sun bumps on his head. Moment two, 1.8 to 3.5s: the sun rolls off and tries to carry him up into the sky, so Bolt grabs it with his long arm, swings it round like a lasso, and ties it to a thin short post made of the cross 十 which snaps up out of the floor. The second 早 is spoken as the sun lands on the post, clicking into the square of 日. Moment three, 3.5 to 5.0s: the sun wobbles on the post, tipping this way and that; Bolt stretches his short arm out uselessly, then his long arm reaches all the way across and steadies it, one clamp on the side of the sun. A tiny sprout of steam from his ears puffs out. Moment four, 5.0s onward: Bolt does a tiny proud wave and pops open the top of his head where a small toast pops up. From 5.0 to 8.0s the glyph is perfectly still and uncovered, and the long arm waves slowly at the bottom of frame while the little toast on his head turns golden, never touching the strokes. Audio: a warm friendly off-screen voice in clear Taiwanese Mandarin says exactly 「早、早、早安」, slowly with clear tones as ㄗㄠˇ、ㄗㄠˇ、ㄗㄠˇ ㄢ. First 早 near 0.7s, second near 2.4s, and 早安 around 5.3s as Bolt waves. Stop after the word. Only soft creaks and a gentle pop, no background music. Soft studio lighting, vivid not neon colors, no flashing, no lens flare, no watermark, no subtitles, no vocabulary text, and no writing other than the single glyph 早.

conceptZh: 披風英雄想把綁著橡皮繩還在打呼的玩具太陽拉上天，布忍者卻躲在小葉子後面拉另一端想留住夜晚，兩人拔河拉到臉紅腳滑，繩子啪一聲鬆開、兩人屁股著地，太陽彈上去壓成「日」，橡皮繩彈直立成「十」，組成「早」。
object: a sleepy round toy sun in a nightcap, tethered to the floor by a long stretchy orange elastic rope
morph: the yanked sun shoots up and squashes into the square 日 on top, while the released elastic rope springs straight and stiff into the tall stem with a short crossbar as the 十 below
creativeAngle: 和前一版「機器人掛太陽」完全不同：改用指定的披風英雄與布忍者，依拔河模式演出。笑點來自英雄想叫太陽起床、忍者想留住黑夜的相反目標，拉長的橡皮繩與蓋住頭的披風提供連續動作，繩子鬆開的瞬間直接把太陽和繩子彈成「早」的上下兩部分，物件與筆畫對應清楚，最後三秒字形完全靜止，英雄在字外揮手說早安。
promptEn:
An 8-second 3D animated toy clip on a clean solid pale cream-yellow backdrop, locked camera, soft studio light. The only text ever on screen is the single Traditional Chinese glyph 早 in saturated sunrise-orange strokes, centered, about 70 percent of frame height: a squarish 日 on top standing directly over a tall 十 below.

Cast: Captain Flop, a chunky plastic action-figure hero with a square jaw, red boots and a flowing red cape three sizes too long that keeps flopping over his own head. Supporting: Pip, a tiny grey felt ninja with button eyes who hides behind a single small leaf that covers only his nose.

0 to 1.5s: a round orange toy sun snores at floor level in a striped nightcap, tethered to the floor by a long stretchy orange elastic rope. Captain Flop zooms in from the left, cape flops over his face, he bonks softly into the sun, boing. He peels the cape off, points up at the sky, grabs the rope and heaves. The first 早 is spoken as he grabs the rope. The sun lifts a little.

1.5 to 3.2s: Pip pops up behind his tiny leaf on the right, button eyes peeking over it, convinced he is invisible. He wants the dark to stay, so he grabs the other end of the rope and yanks the sun back down. Tug-of-war: both lean back, boots skidding, rope stretching into a long trembling orange line across the frame, the sun bouncing in the middle like a bead.

3.2 to 4.6s: both lean so far back they are almost flat, faces turning tomato red, cheeks puffing. The cape flops over Captain Flop's head again and he keeps pulling blind. One frozen beat of quivering tension, then TWANG: the rope lets go. Both fly backward and land on their bottoms at the bottom corners of the frame with a squashy bounce.

4.6 to 5.0s: the sun shoots straight up to the top center and squashes flat into the orange square 日 with its bar across the middle, nightcap popping off and landing beside Pip. The released rope springs stiff and upright directly beneath it as the tall stem, its tangled middle snapping out into the short crossbar of 十. The glyph 早 locks into place, crisp and perfectly readable. The second 早 is spoken exactly as it locks.

5.0 to 8.0s: the glyph stays perfectly still and uncovered. Captain Flop sits up at the bottom left, pushes his cape off his face, stretches a big happy morning stretch and waves a wide good-morning wave up toward the glyph. The word 早安 is spoken exactly on that wave, and the glyph gives one soft warm glow in reply. At the bottom right Pip's smoke bomb finally goes off late, a tiny puff that reveals him completely, and he shrugs. Neither character touches the strokes.

Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice in clear Taiwanese Mandarin says exactly 「早、早、早安」, read slowly and distinctly with clear tones as ㄗㄠˇ、ㄗㄠˇ、ㄗㄠˇ ㄢ. First 早 near 0.9s, second 早 near 4.8s, 早安 near 5.8s. Stop after the word, no other speech. Only soft boings, a rubbery stretch creak and a gentle twang, no music louder than the voice. Bright but not neon colors, no flashing, no lens flare, no watermark, no subtitles, no vocabulary text, and no writing other than the single glyph 早.
